title: Residual-risk statement (DORA Art. 5(2) / ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2)
description: Schema for residual-risk.json, emitted by scripts/validators/risk_acceptance.py (task T-121). It is the machine-readable substrate of the Part D.4 residual-risk statement: an aggregation of the OPEN (Active) accepted ICT risks parsed from docs/compliance/exception-register.md (Part J.2 risk-acceptance / exceptions log), tied to the board-approved risk tolerance. DORA Art. 5(2) requires the management body to determine the appropriate ICT risk tolerance level; ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2 requires board-approved risk-acceptance criteria with a named risk owner per accepted risk. The validator carries the T-33 envelope so the compliance gate (T-30) and matrix consume it uniformly. HONESTY: signed_by_accountable_officer is always false here — the officer's signature is a human act applied at seal time (sign-and-attest), never asserted by the validator.

status.description: T-33 envelope status. PASS only when every Active acceptance is bounded (named approver + named owner + justification + future expiry <=12mo). FAIL on any unbounded/invalid acceptance (spec §8 anti-pattern #5). INDETERMINATE when the register is missing/unparseable.

tier.description: Always BLOCKING — an unbounded risk acceptance is a documented rejection trigger.

measured.description: T-33 measured value: open_count and violation count, or null when INDETERMINATE.

register.description: Path to the source exception register parsed.

errors.description: Human-readable list of unbounded/invalid acceptances (empty on PASS).

open_accepted_risks.description: Count of Active (open) accepted risks. 0 is a valid 'no exceptions noted' state.

status_counts.description: Count of register rows by normalised Status token (active/expired/remediated/...).

soonest_expiry.description: The open risk expiring soonest, or null when no dated open risks exist.

open_risks.description: One entry per Active accepted risk.

board_tolerance.description: Reference block tying residual risk to the board-approved tolerance (DORA Art. 5(2)).

signed_by_accountable_officer.description: ALWAYS false at validation time. The officer signature is applied at seal time (human act); the validator never asserts it.
